procedural_matters: NED 1120 was represented by Esther DE JONG.
SGP 3562 was represented by Nigel TAN.
NED 1120 presented photo evidence of the injury.
The panel of the International Jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
facts: Conditions at the time of the incident were 12 knots of wind with choppy water.
NED 1120 (blue fleet) and SGP 1120 (yellow fleet) were sailing on port tack and on converging courses, with NED 1120 on a close-hauled course and SGP 3562 on a broad reach.
When the boats were approximately 10 boat lengths apart, NED 1120 hailed to SGP 3562 multiple times.
When the distance between the boats was approximately 2 boat lengths, SGP 3562 luffed to a reaching course and immediately thereafter, NED 1120 bore away sharply.
There was contact between the starboard shroud of SGP 3562 and the arm of NED 1120’s crew and between the starboard wing of SGP 3562 and NED 1120’s bow and port wing.
The contact resulted in a 5 cm bruise on NED 1120 crew’s arm, just below elbow.
Immediately after the incident, SGP 3562 was aware she broke RRS 11 but decided not to take a penalty.
conclusions: SGP 3562 to windward failed to keep clear of NED 1120 to leeward, and broke RRS 11.
SGP 3562 did not avoid contact with NED 1120 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).

By knowingly breaking RRS 11 and not taking the appropriate penalty, SGP 3562 failed to compete in compliance with the principles of sportsmanship and fair play as stated in Basic Principles and required by RRS 2. SGP 3562 broke RRS 2.
It was not reasonably possible for NED 1120, the right-of-way boat, to avoid contact with SGP 3562 when it became clear that SGP 3562 was not keeping clear. NED 1120 did not break RRS 14(a).
